sections.h2: Filming the Unboxing vs Starting From a Photo
paras: Cost. A filmed unboxing pays a person, a place, and an edit. Here the clips draw from a monthly plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
Timing. You start when the package photo exists. You do not wait on a booked crew or a studio afternoon. A finished clip can be ready in minutes.
How many clips. One photo feeds the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. Each of those is its own clip, and you can run them side by side.
Who has to be there. One person can make the three clips. Nobody else has to come in.
Another version. A new sentence makes another clip when you want a different opening for the same product.

sections.h2: What Photo Should a Launch Unboxing Start From?
paras: Use a clear photo of the product in the packaging people will receive. Shoot it in daylight, with a plain face of the package toward the camera.

If the box design is still changing, wait until you can photograph the package people will receive. A stand-in box becomes the box shoppers expect. Count what ships. A listing address can fill the first draft. You still replace any photo that is not the package you will mail.
sections.alt: You get the mug beside its mailer. Hands place the cream mug beside the matching kraft parcel and folded tissue.

sections.h2: Which Unboxing Ideas Fit Launch Week?
paras: Plan a teaser, a reveal, and a closer look. Each one uses the same package photo and its own sentence. Use one saved avatar on all three.

The teaser shows the closed box and a hand on the lid. The reveal opens the package and lifts the product out. The closer look turns one detail toward the camera. [Product videos](page:product-videos) fit when you want a demo after the open. [Image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when a photo of the closed box should simply start to move.
sections.alt: You get the start of the open. Hands lift the kraft lid and begin to show the cream mug.

sections.h2: How Do I Write the Scene for Each Launch Clip?
paras: Name the box, the hands, and the one motion. The date and the price go in the caption you type. A drafted script can suggest the line, and you shorten it to that one motion.

The teaser can be hands resting on the lid, in soft daylight. The reveal can lift the lid and raise the product out. The closer look names the one detail you want turned toward the camera. Keep each sentence to one motion.
sections.alt: You get the mug coming out. Hands raise the cream mug, with no lid, from tissue inside the kraft parcel.

sections.h2: What You Can Set on the Launch Clip
paras: You can make the first teaser without opening a timeline app. A photo of the package is the start. There is no film background to learn first.
You can set the tissue color and put your own mark in the corner before you download.
You can pick a quieter voice when the shop's tone is calm, before the reveal goes up.
A monthly plan covers the set, so the teaser and the reveal do not each need a new quote from a crew.
The reveal can use the face from the teaser, so the next post does not introduce someone new.
Edit the draft so the spoken line matches the one motion in the clip. You decide the final words. The same line can be spoken in another language for a second market.

sections.h2: How Long Should a Launch Unboxing Be?
paras: Use 6 seconds for the teaser, and 10 seconds to open and show the product. Use 15 seconds for a slower reveal, and 30 seconds when the box holds more than one item.

In that same order, they cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before each clip starts. Each length is its own clip. Make the length you need for [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok). Make a longer one if the product page should show more of the unboxing.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Launch Unboxing
paras: A home shop shows an avatar lifting the product out and naming the size that ships. They post that teaser before the page is live.
A gift shop shows the tissue, then the product, in that order. The closed box is the teaser and the lid lift is the reveal.
A two-person shop makes all three clips from one package photo between orders, and checks the product against the real box.
A kitchen shop keeps the voice on the one product in the box. It does not name a second item the buyer will not find.
Use one real package photo, one saved avatar, and three sentences, for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. You add your own date and price.
Show only the box and the product the buyer will receive. After you check the unboxing, send it to TikTok or Facebook, or download it.

faq.q: How is an AI unboxing video different from filming one?
faq.a: An AI unboxing video starts from your product photos, so you can make it in minutes without a camera crew. You can try another version without booking a new shoot.

faq.q: Can a product link start an unboxing video?
faq.a: Yes. Paste your product link to bring in its photos and details. Check that the package and contents in the video match what you ship.

faq.q: What if the unboxing video shows the wrong item?
faq.a: Make a new version using clearer photos and a description of the exact box contents. Check the finished video against the package customers will receive.

faq.q: What if my packaging changes before launch?
faq.a: Use a photo of the final package customers will receive. If the packaging changes, make a new video so shoppers see the right box.

faq.q: Can an unboxing video show how my product works?
faq.a: Yes. Show the product coming out of the package, then show it in use. You can make the video without filming a separate demo.

faq.q: How can video help sell a new product?
faq.a: A short video shows shoppers what arrives and how it works before they buy. Start from a product photo or link and make a launch video in minutes.

faq.q: How can I make an unboxing video with AI?
faq.a: Upload a clear photo of your package and product, then choose a style and AI actor. Describe the unboxing and check that the video shows what customers will receive.

faq.q: How long should an unboxing video be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds based on how much you need to show. A short video can reveal one item; use a longer one for several.

faq.q: How many credits does an unboxing video cost?
faq.a: A 6-second video costs 24 credits; 10 seconds costs 40, 15 costs 60, and 30 costs 120. If generation fails, your credits return.

faq.q: How can the unboxing video sound like my shop?
faq.a: Use the same simple words you use in your product descriptions and social posts. Choose a voice that suits your brand and check the message before downloading.

faq.q: Can I change the voice, music, and captions?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a different voice, music, or captions before you download the video. Check any price, date, or discount code before posting.

faq.q: Which photo should I use for an AI unboxing video?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo that clearly shows the package and every item inside. This helps the video show the right product and a believable reveal.

faq.q: Can one package photo make several launch videos?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the photo and try different introductions, voices, or product details. You can compare several videos without another shoot.

faq.q: Can I post the unboxing video on TikTok or Facebook?
faq.a: Yes. Download the video without a watermark and post it on TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram. Choose a size that fits the platform.
